analysis:
Examined both documentation excerpts and the changed-range map. The new Gemma TP section (docs/architecture/inference.md:4038–4240) describes verified artifact reads, rank load agreements, authenticated collectives, coordinated cancellation, per-lane memory admission, and default-on memory/encrypted-SSD prefix reuse. Placement changes rank predicted performance rather than replacing load admission. No concrete security regression is established by these documentation changes; the runtime implementations and BASE behavior are not supplied.
Relevant contracts are A-001/A-003 confidentiality, A-004 model integrity, A-016/A-017 authorization and qualification, TB-002/TB-007/TB-011, T-007/T-010/T-027/T-028 and T-041. Integration should inspect Gemma4TensorParallelVerifiedLoad, LoadAgreement, RequestBudget, RequestLoop and Prefix implementations named at lines 4100–4166: confirm verified reads, bounded authenticated frames, cancellation/drain behavior, tenant scope propagation to both ranks and disk records, and current authorization checks before serving. In particular, the new memory tier/default-on prefix description at 4108–4111 and 4145–4164 needs reconciliation with T-041's production SSD-only/no persistent RAM tier posture. It may be a separately gated cluster candidate; these excerpts do not establish production activation or missing tenant isolation.
Also examined surrounding Qwen budgeting and precision caveats (4003–4036), and unchanged GLM media, token-credit, transport, qualification, KV precision and SSD encoding descriptions (4242–4511). They describe fail-closed transport, bounded media handling, paired stop agreement, and precision-bound load agreements; they do not independently verify the new Gemma implementation. Review the generalized TensorParallelSwitchLinear interaction with Qwen and Gemma, numerical qualification, and cluster serving authorization in the source batches. Remaining uncertainty is material implementation coverage, not evidence of a vulnerability.
